flags.quote: Moving your c8-bishop to b7 is playable, but moving your pawn to d5 would be better because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: I play ...d5 and I am not taking a pawn. White can take on d5. The real idea is hitting the center while White has wasted a tempo on f3, not a hypothetical capture that never happens on this move.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c5 is the strongest move because you control more central squares.
flags.critique: The reasons list includes backward_pawn and then the sentence pretends this is just more center. ...c5 asks White what to do with d4, and it can leave me with a backward d6 pawn. Also you called a 45-centipawn drop the strongest move.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This is the move that clamps the position: space, a locked center, and my light-squared bishop staring at granite. You gave me a blank strongest-move stamp. If you only explain one pawn push in this game, explain this one.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d5 with your c-pawn is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: That pawn is defended by the bishop on b7 and the knight on f6. This is a recapture in a pawn trade, not winning an undefended pawn. wins_material on equal exchanges trains me to stop counting.

flags.quote: Moving your d7-knight to e5 is playable, but moving your pawn to g6 would be better.
flags.critique: Better than a knight on e5, and you will not tell me why. g6 does what, stop Nf5? Prepare a bishop? I cannot use an alternative that is just a SAN code.

flags.quote: Moving your e2-bishop to b5 is the strongest move because it forces the king to respond.
flags.critique: Check does not force the king to do anything. I can block six different ways, and the game actually blocked with a knight. This is the check phrase-bank lying about how checks work.

flags.quote: Castling kingside keeps you winning because it gives your king shelter and brings your rook closer to the center. A better move would have been moving your g3-knight to f5.
flags.critique: So I am still winning, there is better, and the better move is Nf5 with zero reason. Nf5 is an outpost hitting d6 and e7. Castling is the same generic shelter-and-rook sentence you paste on every O-O.

flags.quote: Moving your b5-bishop to d3 is the strongest move because it saves your d3-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: The bishop is on b5. ...a6 is kicking it. Calling it your d3-bishop is the destination square leaking into the identity. I know which piece I just moved. Don't rename it after the square it fled to.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on b5 with your c3-knight puts it where the black pawn can take and you lose the exchange.
flags.critique: A pawn takes my knight. That is a piece, not the exchange. SEE recapture math (axb5 Bxb5 nets about two pawns) should not teach me the wrong word for rook-for-minor-piece. a4 is also dumped on me with no idea attached.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on b5 with your a-pawn is the strongest move because you come out a bishop ahead and it unveils an attack from your rook on the white pawn.
flags.critique: I took a knight with a pawn. I am a knight for a pawn ahead, not a bishop. The rook opening on a2 is real. The material label is a lie, and I will notice because I can count.

flags.quote: You are still winning, but taking the bishop on b5 with your a6-bishop puts it where the white queen can take and you lose a knight. A better move would have been moving your pawn to c4 because it saves your a6-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: Queen takes bishop is a bishop trade. The d7 knight is still defended three times. I do not lose a knight. And ...c4 is not a save: it forks the queen on d3 and the bishop on b5. You turned a pawn fork into a timid 'save your bishop.'

flags.quote: Moving your a8-rook to a5 is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: I just attacked the queen on b5. That is the whole move. a2 can still walk to a3 or a4, so it is not even a pin. You buried a hanging queen under a fake pawn pin.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to f5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: You had Nf5 as the improvement two moves ago and now that I play it, silence. Outpost, hits d6/e7/g7/h6. This is the kind of square a 1200 is trying to learn to occupy, and you shrugged.

flags.quote: Moving your f1-rook to b1 is playable, but moving your pawn to a6 would be better because it gives you a passed pawn.
flags.critique: The a-pawn has been passed since ...axb5. a6 does not give me a passed pawn. It pushes one I already have. Rfb1 is about the b-file. Don't sell pawn advances as if the passer was born this ply.

flags.quote: Moving your e5-knight to d3 is the strongest move because it overloads the white queen.
flags.critique: The knight attacks the queen on e1 and the f2 pawn. That is a fork-ish outpost, not an overload. Overload means one piece is defending two things it cannot both save. Stop using that word as wallpaper.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your queen to d1 leaves your queen overloaded. A better move would have been moving your bishop to c3 because you fork the black f6-knight and the black queen and then fork the black d3-knight and the black queen.
flags.critique: Bc3 attacks the queen and the f6 knight. It does not attack d3. You glued two fork clauses into nonsense. Also 'leaves your queen overloaded' teaches me nothing about what Qd1 actually failed to do.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g6 is the strongest move because it overloads the white queen.
flags.critique: ...g6 kicks the knight on f5. A pawn attacks a piece. If you cannot say 'you kick the knight,' take the coaching badge off. Overload of the queen is not on this board.

flags.quote: Moving your knight to h6 doesn't ease a difficult position because it saves your knight from capture. A better move would have been moving your rook to b1 because you can likely take a bishop.
flags.critique: The check is a blunder because it saves the knight? That sentence eats itself. The knight runs from ...g6 into a silly check on h6, and my king will just walk up and look at it. Rb1 hits my queen. 'Likely take a bishop' is Nxe7, which was already available and is not why Rb1 is the move.

flags.quote: Moving your king to g7 is the strongest move because it overloads the white queen.
flags.critique: I stepped out of check and my king attacks the knight on h6. That is the lesson: the check was free and the knight is hanging. You said overload again. pawn_shield is in the reasons for a king walking onto the knight. I cannot learn from this.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your bishop to e3 makes your king easier to attack. A better move would have been moving your rook to a4.
flags.critique: Lichess called this an inaccuracy. You called it a blunder, which matches the 473-centipawn hole, then explained it as king safety. The bishop left d2 and opened the second rank for my queen toward g2. Say that. Ra4 with no because-clause is another SAN I am supposed to memorize.

flags.quote: Moving your d3-knight to b4 is a blunder, but taking the pawn on d5 with your f6-knight would be better.
flags.critique: A 609-centipawn swing and you give me 'but Nxd5 would be better.' I pulled a monster knight off d3. Nxd5 grabs the protected passed pawn. Lichess says mistake, you say blunder, and neither of us gets a sentence about the actual tactic.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but taking the pawn on c5 with your bishop puts it where the black pawn can take and you lose a knight. A better move would have been moving your queen to c1 because you can likely take a queen.
flags.critique: ...dxc5 is bishop for pawn. The knight I lose is the one on h6 that has been hanging to my king since Nh6+. You glued the wrong capture to the hanging piece. And Qc1 attacks an undefended queen on b2. Drop 'likely.' It is hanging.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d6 is the strongest move because it gives you a passed pawn.
flags.critique: 257 centipawns gone, ignored_threat in the reasons, and you still say strongest. The d-pawn was already passed. You are pushing it while something else is hanging. If the engine UCI matched, do not let that override a two-pawn swing in the sentence I read.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to d6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: 356 centipawns, three ignored_threat reasons, empty because-clause, classified best. The queen walks onto d6 and the next trick is I take on d7. Strongest is a lie. At least name one of the threats you admit I ignored.

flags.quote: Taking the rook on d7 with your queen is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the king and you take the defender of the black bishop.
flags.critique: The rook is protected by the knight. I take it, my queen sits on d7, and ...Nxd7 wins the queen. 813 centipawns. You called it best and rambled about a pin and a bishop defender. This is the worst sentence in the game. I hung a queen for a rook and you congratulated me.

suggestions.title: Block wins_material on equal recaptures
suggestions.detail: Ply 19 said cxd5 wins an undefended pawn that two pieces defend. wins_material with seeCp near the captured pawn's value fires on recaptures. Gate that reason unless net SEE stays positive after the opponent's recapture, or require the captured unit to have zero defenders. A 1200 notices immediately when a trade is called a free pawn.

suggestions.title: Stop mapping knight-for-pawn SEE to exchange or bishop
suggestions.detail: hangingLossCopy treats 180-220 SEE as 'the exchange' (ply 27 Nxb5). materialLabel treats ~200 as 'a bishop' (ply 28 axb5). Both are pawn-takes-knight plus a recapture. Label from the hanging piece type when a pawn is the attacker, or say 'a piece for a pawn.' Nobody at 1200 will trust a coach who calls a hung knight the exchange.

suggestions.title: Require two undefended targets before saying overload
suggestions.detail: Overload was the because-clause for Nd3 (attacks the queen), ...g6 (kicks Nf5), ...Kg7 (king takes the checking knight), and Qd1. pickBenefitReasons is letting overload outrank kicked_by_pawn, hanging, and fork. Only emit overload when the defender actually watches two hanging units. This one detector poisoned the whole late game.

suggestions.title: Do not teach suggested moves as likely captures
suggestions.detail: capture.likely produced 'you can likely take a pawn' for ...d5 (ply 8), a bishop for Rb1 (ply 57), and a queen for Qc1 (ply 61). On ply 61 the queen on b2 has zero defenders, so 'likely' is cowardly. verifyLikelyTactics should stay out of the because-clause unless the suggested SAN is itself a capture this ply. Threaten/attack copy already exists in hanging and fork.

suggestions.title: Do not say strongest when eval loss is huge
suggestions.detail: classifyPlayedMove stamps best whenever UCI matches the top engine move. That printed strongest on d6 (257), d7 (232), Qd6 (356), and Qxd7 (813) while ignored_threat sat in the reasons. Cap the UCI override at goodMaxLossCp (50) for copy, or switch the template to 'the engine still likes this' instead of 'strongest move' when loss is a pawn or more. Ply 71 called hanging a queen the strongest move.

suggestions.title: Rank attacks on queens above relative pawn pins
suggestions.detail: Ra5 (ply 34) attacks the queen on b5 and you said 'pin the pawn to the rook.' Same pin sentence on Ra7 and Be3. selectBecauseReasons prefers pin because it is tactical, even when the pinned unit can still march down the file. If a move attacks a queen or saves a hanging rook, that reason wins. Pin copy also needs the pinned piece to be unable to move off the line.

suggestions.title: Name saved pieces from the square they left
suggestions.detail: Bd3 'saves your d3-bishop from capture' (ply 25): labeledPiece uses the unit square after the move. saves_piece should keep the from-square (b5-bishop). Same class of bug as destination leaking into identity. Cheap fix, high eye-roll.

suggestions.title: Never emit a better-move SAN with an empty because
suggestions.detail: g6, Nfd7, Nf5, Qd7, Rb3, a4, Ra4, Nxd5 all appeared as improvements with no reason or with a leftover reason from the played move. missedImprovementSentence should refuse to print the alternative unless suggestedBecause is non-null. Better to say 'the engine prefers d5' than 'd5 would be better' and stop. Also stop pasting center_control on every opening ply (d4, Nf6, c4, Nc3, e4, d6) when the reason list is only that.

whatWorked: Ply 6 actually named the Nimzo idea: ...Bb4 pins the knight to the king instead of ...b6.
Ply 30 ...Ba6: pin the bishop to the rook is the real tactic and the sentence is usable.
Ply 35 Qe2 and ply 49 Bd2: hanging queen / hanging b2-pawn, stated plainly.
Ply 50 ...Rxb2 combines an undefended pawn with a pin on the 2nd rank without inventing a piece.
Ply 67 Rb1 names the skewer on the queen and the knight behind it.
